clue.text: Stop one guy importing first of things for elementary arrangement

parts.note: a period is a full stop, the punctuation mark
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: importing means the guy takes something into itself

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about halting and bringing in a rope, apparently for some basic layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' sets T, the first of 'things', inside CABLE, just after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of chemical elements is literally an arrangement of the elements, punned as 'elementary'.

clue.text: Arrangement for continuation of leaders routing empire, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A plan for keeping rulers in power by steering an empire somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the rearrangement of ROUTING EMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inheritance by the eldest son is a system that hands leadership on through each generation.

clue.text: Initially used for sleep, otherwise promoting rest

indicators.note: otherwise says the gathered letters are to be set out in a different order
Initially takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Something first used for sleep turns out to encourage relaxation too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges U (the first of 'used') with FOR and SLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restful or calming encourages repose, the quiet state of resting.

clue.text: More than one flower like 4, golden, comes up

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to come up is to rise, as the sun rises

explanation.surface: Golden flowers like irises push up out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 is the answer to 4 down, IRIS; the orris is a kind of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a species of iris whose root gives a violet-scented powder, so the plural names several such blooms.

clue.text: Assistant virtually picked up flower

indicators.note: picked up, in a down clue, means the word is lifted and read bottom to top

parts.note: Siri is Apple's virtual assistant

explanation.surface: A helper all but gathered up a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' reads as 'almost' but belongs with 'Assistant' to name a virtual assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a common garden bloom with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Broadcast live on set involving current set

indicators.note: involving means the scrambled letters take something in
Broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A live broadcast on a film set involves the current set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' scrambles LIVE ON SET, and 'involving' adds I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV set is a television receiver, so set can stand for it.

clue.text: Feline speed will involve such running

indicators.note: will involve says the first part wraps around the second

parts.note: bat means speed, as in going at a fair bat

indicators.note: running means the letters of the word such are loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat's speed depends on that kind of running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' and 'will involve' are the signals; 'speed' looks like part of the cat picture but supplies letters, from the British idiom 'at a fair bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The serval is called the bush-cat, an African wild feline.

clue.text: One individual upset about verse and conclusion to verse

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes around another piece
upset, in a down clue, turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the single-letter pronoun for an individual self

explanation.surface: A lone person is upset over a poem and how it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ONE into ENO, and 'about' puts V inside to give ENVO, with I after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, addressing the reader or patron.

clue.text: Tell nearly everything about Independent, balancing positive and negative?

indicators.note: about says the joined pieces go round the abbreviation

parts.note: to impart is to tell or pass on news

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A question of reporting fully on the Independent newspaper, being fair to both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL to AL; IMPART and AL together go 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being even-handed means weighing the case for and against equally.

clue.text: Attacked, though, yielding silver, spared

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so letters are surrendered from the word

parts.note: savaged means attacked fiercely
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone attacked but, by handing over silver, was let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' takes AG out of SAVAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone is to rescue them from harm or punishment, a synonym.

clue.text: Iran President arranged evening events

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The Iranian head of state organised some evening functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges IRAN PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Social gatherings for a meal held at night are typical evening occasions.

clue.text: Honours son after accepting son's rule

indicators.note: after places the lone son at the end
accepting means the honours take another letter in

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, Officers of the Order of the British Empire
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Honours for a son, following one for his son, seem to govern the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts S into OBES, and 'after' adds the other S at the end. OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation can rule or dominate one's thoughts, which is what it means to preoccupy them.

clue.text: English opinion not against expulsion

indicators.note: not says the following word's sense is left out of the opinion

parts.note: a conviction is a firmly held opinion
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An English view that is not opposed to throwing someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not against' removes CON from CONVICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown out of a home by a landlord is a forced removal, a kind of expulsion.

clue.text: Sudden jerk audibly does for winter transport

parts.note: a bob is a quick jerky movement

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard rather than read, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to do for someone is to kill them, to slay

explanation.surface: A sudden jolt is apparently what finishes someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' applies to 'does for', heard as SLAYS and written SLEIGHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing toboggans used on ice tracks are vehicles for snowy weather.

clue.text: French are enshrining France's first union in literary outpourings

indicators.note: enshrining means holding something within, like a relic in a shrine

parts.note: es is French for 'are', as in tu es

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: fusion is a union or merging

explanation.surface: The French have enshrined a union with France in gushing writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French are' means the French word for 'are', not the French people; 'enshrining' and 'first' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive writing pours out feeling unrestrainedly, so the plural names such gushing passages.

clue.text: Corps engaged in sincere termination of fighting

indicators.note: engaged in means the military letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: true means sincere, as a true friend
C is the abbreviation for Corps, as in RAMC

explanation.surface: An army corps sincerely committed to a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' puts C inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire agreement brings hostilities to a halt, at least for a while.

clue.text: Total expert penning new expression

parts.note: utter means total, as in utter nonsense

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals are penned

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A complete expert writing a fresh phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads like writing, but it means N is shut inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything spoken aloud, a word or remark, counts as a vocal expression.

clue.text: I'd gone first, and just ran

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped to give the letters
led means went in front, gone first

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of going first and merely running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just ran' is the engine's sense: ticking over without moving.
explanation.definitionFit: An idling engine is running but doing no work, merely ticking over.

clue.text: Overwhelmed daughter argued about source of noise

indicators.note: about says the argued word goes round a letter

parts.note: rowed, rhyming with cowed, means quarrelled

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A daughter swamped by a quarrel over where the racket came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N, the 'source of noise', inside ROWED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swamped, by water or by a flood of anything, is to be overwhelmed.

clue.text: Baseball player's sports clothes?

parts.note: the fielding position, split in two, reads as a pair of sporting garments, legwear plus an upper garment

explanation.surface: What a baseball player wears to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as SHORTS and TOP, a sports outfit; the whole is a fielder between second and third base.
explanation.definitionFit: This infield position in baseball sits between second and third base.

clue.text: Goes over the evacuated Italian port

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: goes, as in has a go, means tries

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Someone passes over an emptied Italian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties THE to TE, and 'over' puts TRIES above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a city and seaport in north-east Italy on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Where you regularly go to be enthralled by nude dancing, being released

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside
dancing means the letters of nude are jumbled

parts.note: loos are toilets, the places you go regularly

explanation.surface: A place you visit often to be captivated by naked dancing, now letting you go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' gives UNED, and 'enthralled by' is the container signal. LOO is the everyday British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unloosed is to be set free or untied, a form of release.

clue.text: Prisoner, one fellow held by the French King

indicators.note: held by means the pieces are gripped inside

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
the Roman numeral for one
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A convict, a man held by the French king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts I and F inside LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is someone serving a life sentence in jail.

clue.text: One reflects the writer's backing nothing in a basic education?

indicators.note: backing means the contraction is read the other way round

parts.note: the writer is I, so the writer's (is) gives I'm

indicators.note: in places the zero within the three letters

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are a basic education
O is the zero for nothing

explanation.surface: A writer mulls over a background lacking even basic schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' and 'in' are the signals. The 'three Rs' (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the traditional British shorthand for basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass throws back light and images, so it is something that reflects.

clue.text: Performed with old opera heroine

parts.note: did means performed, as a task

explanation.surface: An old operatic heroine was performed again.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido is the queen of Carthage in Purcell's Dido and Aeneas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido, queen of Carthage, is the tragic title character of Purcell's opera.

clue.text: Slight contribution to novel finale

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small part played in the ending of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf, so slight in build.

clue.text: Musical figurations, mostly smooth, encapsulating one's polish

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing other letters as in a capsule
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: glib means smooth-talking
one's, as one is, gives is
to sand is to polish a surface

explanation.surface: Musical flourishes, almost slick, wrapping up someone's polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves GLI, and 'encapsulating' splits it between L and I; 'polish' reads as a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandos are sweeping slides up or down a scale, a kind of ornamental passage.

clue.text: They again unearth reservation about recording covering Queen

indicators.note: about means the reservation's letters go around the rest

parts.note: a disc is a recording
over can mean covering, as a lid over a pot
ER is the royal cipher for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A booking concerns a record with the Queen on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, and 'covering' is not a second container but supplies letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: People who find something lost a second time unearth it anew, finding again what was once found.
